chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Hashim from Isma'il b. Marar from Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman from Abu Ayyub from Abu Hamza from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:

All goodness is gathered in three traits: sight, silence, and speech. Every sight devoid of contemplation is negligence. Every silence devoid of thought is heedlessness. Every speech devoid of remembrance [of Allah] is prattle. Blessed is he whose sight is a lesson, whose silence is contemplation, whose speech is remembrance, who cries over his sins, and from whose evil people are safe.

key_terms.اعتبار: contemplation - reflecting and drawing lessons from what one sees
key_terms.طوبى: blessed - a tree in paradise, denoting supreme happiness
key_terms.غفلة: heedlessness - state of being oblivious to spiritual realities
key_terms.لغو: prattle/vain talk - speech that contains no remembrance of Allah

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the three traits that encompass all goodness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam Ali (AS) summarizes all goodness in three traits: mindful seeing, thoughtful silence, and speech filled with divine remembrance. This teaching was recorded in the 23rd assembly session held on Tuesday, two nights into Shawwal 367 AH, reflecting a core principle of Islamic self-discipline where every moment of awareness should be directed toward spiritual benefit.
